raw_findings.body: Because the translate accelerator only loads config.locale on demand and the fallback locales are loaded solely by this controller hook, the fallback locale's YAML is never loaded outside a web request, so the lookup returns a 'translation missing' result instead of the fallback translation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Missing translations silently render as untranslated keys in emails and background-generated content.
raw_findings.impact: Because the translate accelerator only loads config.locale on demand and the fallback locales are loaded solely by this controller hook, the fallback locale's YAML is never loaded outside a web request, so the lookup returns a 'translation missing' result instead of the fallback translation.
raw_findings.root_cause: Fallback-locale preloading was wired only into the controller's set_locale, while the on-demand loader in translate_accelerator loads just config.locale.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Invoke I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load the fallback chain inside load_locale/translate) from the shared locale-setting path used by jobs and mailers, not only from the web controller.
raw_findings.title: Fallback locales never loaded for non-HTTP translation contexts
raw_findings.trigger: A background job, mailer (e.g. UserNotifications), or rake task translates a key that is missing in the active locale and must fall back to SiteSetting.default_locale or :en, without ever passing through ApplicationController#set_locale.

raw_findings.body: The pre-existing LRU cache keys entries by "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}", which does not include default_locale; fallback results computed from FallbackLocale#[] (which depends on SiteSetting.default_locale) remain cached and stale until an I18n.reload!.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale fallback translations are served after a default-locale change.
raw_findings.impact: The pre-existing LRU cache keys entries by "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}", which does not include default_locale; fallback results computed from FallbackLocale#[] (which depends on SiteSetting.default_locale) remain cached and stale until an I18n.reload!.
raw_findings.root_cause: Introducing default_locale-dependent fallbacks over a cache whose key does not account for the fallback ordering.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Incorporate the fallback chain / default_locale into the cache key, or invalidate the translation cache when SiteSetting.default_locale changes.
raw_findings.title: Translation LRU cache key omits fallback determinant (default_locale)
raw_findings.trigger: An admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale at runtime after some keys missing in a user locale have already been resolved through the old fallback chain and cached.

raw_findings.body: The fallback chain (user locale, site default, :en) and the on-demand loading of fallback locales are unverified, so behavioral regressions can merge undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review quality gap: fallback behavior lacks automated verification.
raw_findings.impact: The fallback chain (user locale, site default, :en) and the on-demand loading of fallback locales are unverified, so behavioral regressions can merge undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Feature code (FallbackLocaleList, ensure_loaded!) was introduced with no accompanying spec.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a spec asserting that translating a key missing in a non-English locale falls back to SiteSetting.default_locale then :en, and that ensure_loaded! loads the fallback locales.
raw_findings.title: New server-side fallback feature added without test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: Regression in FallbackLocaleList#[] ordering, ensure_loaded! loading, or the translate accelerator's ensure_loaded! interaction would not be caught by CI.

The patch adds ensure_loaded! to the controller, but translate_accelerator.rb already has I18n.ensure_loaded! method (line 62-65) that can be called from anywhere. No evidence that background jobs/mailers don't set locale properly or that this causes actual translation failures. The candidate assumes mailers/jobs never call ensure_loaded! but provides no proof.
